facts.statement: The genus Dallasiella was described by Cappetta and Case in 1999.
The type species of the genus Dallasiella is Dallasiella willistoni.
The genus Dallasiella contains two valid species: Dallasiella brachyodon and Dallasiella willistoni.
facts.quote: subdivision: Dallasiella brachyodon Siversson, Cederström, & Ryan, 2022 Dallasiella willistoni Cappetta & Case, 1999

facts.statement: Fossils of Dallasiella species have been found in North America and Europe.
facts.quote: It contains two valid species, D. willistoni and D. brachyodon, which have been found in North America and Europe.

facts.statement: Dallasiella is currently classified as Lamniformes incertae sedis, having previously been placed in the families Cretoxyrhinidae and Archaeolamnidae.
facts.quote: While formerly placed in the families Cretoxyrhinidae and Archaeolamnidae, it is now considered Lamniformes incertae sedis.

facts.statement: Dallasiella lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Dallasiella is an extinct genus of mackerel sharks that lived during the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Dallasiella lived from the Albian to the Campanian stages, between 113.2 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Campanian (113.2 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Dallasiella belongs to the parent group Lamniformes.
Dallasiella is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
